evaluation_title: Fixed Chronological Split vs. 5-Year Rolling Window Comparative Analysis

key_observations.description: Model hierarchies remain 100% consistent across both evaluation regimes: 1. Hist_Gradient_Boosting, 2. Random_Forest, 3. Ridge_Regression. This proves that tree-based gradient boosting superiority is not an artifact of a single validation split.

The original fixed 2024 validation set produced higher RMSEs (~2.37-2.58 °C) across all models due to anomalous 2024 global summer heatwaves. In contrast, the rolling window mean RMSE (~1.74 °C) provides a more representative expectation of long-term operational performance.

key_observations.point: Training Window Length Sensitivity (8 Years vs. 5 Years on 2024)
key_observations.description: Comparing Fixed 2024 Val (trained on 8 years 2016-2023) against Rolling Fold 4 Val (trained on 5 years 2019-2023): Hist_Gradient_Boosting had 2.370 °C RMSE with 8 years vs. 2.414 °C with 5 years. Additional historical training years provide a modest ~0.04 °C error reduction, indicating that recent 5-year climatological cycles capture the vast majority of UHI dynamics.
Year 2025 was completely excluded from all rolling window fold generation, model training, and stability analysis. It remains an unpolluted, virgin test set for final publication validation.

limitations_and_sources_of_variation: Extreme climate anomalies (e.g. 2024 global heatwaves) induce temporal non-stationarity.
Cloud-mask missingness varies seasonally across monsoon and high-latitude winter months.
Rural reference buffers experience seasonal vegetative green-up/senescence cycles that differ from urban built surfaces.
